issue: PMAT-212/213/214 — four defects the operator found running forjar against the fleet and declared P0: drift -f answered about machines its config never declares and judged them against the local filesystem (#488, #485), a task whose command exits non-zero latched with no way back (#487), and the cargo check could not see what the cargo install wrote (#489)

lanes: two paiml-impl-worker phases, every acceptance command re-run by the orchestrator
quorum.kill_rule: a lane verdict is a claim; all three FAILs were re-run against the real binary before anything was changed, two reproduced and are fixed, one is answered in the evidence and the PR body
quorum.rounds: three lanes at 9ad01216: 3 FAIL. Two findings reproduced (the --dry-run bypass, found independently by lanes 2 and 3; the CARGO_HOME shadowing, found by lane 2) and are fixed in 733804f4. The bundling objection is answered, not accepted.
refuted_claims: The branch introduced a guard against a false green and left the same false green reachable through --dry-run: cmd_drift_dry_run calls the state-dir walk directly rather than through collect_machine_locks where the guard sat, so `drift --dry-run -m <undeclared>` printed '0 resource(s) would be checked' and exited 0. Two of three lanes found it independently; it reproduced; the refusal now runs in both doors. The four original cases missed it because none exercised -m at all.

The rustup bootstrap block still hard-coded $HOME/.cargo/bin after the new prelude prepended ${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin. Measured with CARGO_HOME=/opt/toolchain, the hard-coded export put $HOME/.cargo/bin ahead of the directory rustup actually installs into. Both lines now use the same expression.

One lane refused the branch for carrying three tickets. Accurate about PMAT-212's ticket text and deliberate: the operator declared four issues P0 with the fleet blocked, and the self-hosted pool was measured at 14 of 16 runners busy, so three PRs would serialise three CI passes. Each ticket keeps its own commit, receipt, falsification test and roadmap row; answered in the PR body rather than left implicit.

crux.verdict: three of the four systems surveyed for the latch keep no failure verdict at all, so it is a defect they cannot have; Terraform is the one that persists a verdict and its way back is a forced destroy-and-recreate rather than a re-read. forjar had the persistence and no release of any kind. On scoping, three of four bound a state query to its target BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why none needed an --all-stacks opt-out. On the environment, four of four bind check and action to one environment by construction or one named declaration.
